messages:
maya: Heads-up: i'm sketching two patterns for first-run guidance — (A) a compact floating "Get started" pill that expands to a checklist, or (B) an inline hint system that surfaces tips next to the area youre stuck. which do we prefer for engineers + PMs trying the console?
chris: my vote: pill. predictable, discoverable, low friction to onboard. inline hints can be missed. :white_check_mark:
anita: Pill is better for keyboard & screen reader discoverability. Inline hints often never get keyboard focus unless we explicitly add anchors.
leo: Concern: pill uses corner real estate on small screens. solution: collapsed icon only on <= 640px, full pill on desktop.
sarah: wording matters — avoid the word "tour". Options: "Get started", "Quickstart", "Onboarding helper". "Get started" is clear and action-oriented.
jamal: add a tiny preferences control so users can snooze helper for 7/30 days. otherwise power users complain instantly.
maya: good call. also thinking tiers: quick checklist + samples first, billing second. we want immediate payoff.
chris: checklist draft: 1) Create API key 2) Run sample request 3) Deploy sample project 4) Set billing guard. short bullets.
anita: accessibility nits: status badges need text labels ("Complete"/"Incomplete") not just color. make them focusable with role="status" updates.
leo: tech note: preload minimal sample metadata so opening is instant. metadata budget ~50-100KB gzipped.
sarah: sample CTA copy: "Run sample app" vs "Try sample app" — "Run" suggests immediacy. maybe "Run sample" is even shorter.
maya: "Run sample" + show inline spinner and a small success toast like "Sample started — opened workspace".
anita: keyboard flow proposal: focus lands on pill, Enter to open, focus trap inside panel, Escape closes, first focus on checklist. include shortcut discoverability in command palette.
chris: hybrid idea: pill + contextual nudges only for failing flows (e.g., missing API key). must throttle to avoid nagging.
jamal: telemetry/privacy: any failure-based nudges must be explicit opt-in in settings. and log minimal context only (no API keys or PII).
sarah: visual layout: panel with two tabs: "Quickstart" (checklist + samples) and "Diagnose" (one-click fixes + logs). keep it simple 2-column on desktop, stacked on mobile.
leo: rollout plan: feature flag, 10% new accounts for 2 weeks, metric goals: time-to-first-sample-run, checklist completion, support ticket reduction.
maya: success targets idea: 25-35% checklist complete within 7 days, and 10-20% lower starter support messages.
chris: dev followups: add flag + telemetry events: onboarding.pill.open, onboarding.sample.run, onboarding.checklist.item.complete.
anita: a11y acceptance criteria i'll add to PR: keyboard-only walkthrough, screen reader announcements for open/close and status updates, contrast checks for pill/button (AA).
jamal: QA note: make sure panel opening doesn't shift page layout. use fixed positioning inside a portal.
sarah: copy task: i'll write microcopy variants for the pill label, checklist items, success toasts, and tiny helper tooltip. will post PR.
maya: i'll post Figma comps for pill vs inline hints. please weigh in on the frames. tagging design-review for next Wed.
design-bot: Figma frames uploaded — https://www.figma.com/file/abc/onboard-pill-vs-inline (preview).
leo: rough estimate: 3 dev days + 1 qa day + design polish.
maya: thanks all. last sanity check: do we add a small "Import project" button in the panel or keep only samples?
chris: include both. "Run sample" primary, "Import project" secondary. keeps power users happy.
anita: ensure secondary button is keyboard reachable and labeled clearly (e.g., aria-label="Import existing project").
maya: perfect. i'm turning these notes into the spec now. :sparkles:
